title: Combined RAG + agent quickstart: retrieval as a tool + prompt-injection/tool-misuse guardrails
author: Sabrina James
release_notes: Adds the combined RAG+agent quickstart template (planner/executor) with retrieval implemented as a tool, safe tool defaults, prompt injection mitigations, and end-to-end observability wiring compatible with the quickstart telemetry contract v1.
body: Summary: This PR adds the Combined RAG+Agent template (v1) to the redwood-quickstarts monorepo. The goal is a production-shaped example that demonstrates: (1) an agent loop with tool calling, (2) retrieval implemented as a first-class tool (RAG), and (3) safety/guardrails against prompt injection + tool misuse. The template is designed to run locally in <15 minutes, with a clear path to Docker/Kubernetes deployment and compatibility with Redwood Console dashboards (request correlation, token-cost attribution, error taxonomy). Motivation / context: We have separate RAG and Agents templates already; customers and internal dogfooders keep asking for the combined workflow ("agent can decide to retrieve" + tool-based grounding). This PR is the baseline implementation for ENG-2844 and aligns with the tool calling guidelines + telemetry contract (ENG-2845). Key behaviors: Planner/executor loop: the model produces a structured "plan" object (JSON) and then executes steps; when a step requires knowledge, the agent calls the retrieval tool. Retrieval as a tool: "retrieve" tool takes a query + optional filters, performs embedding + vector search, returns top_k chunks with source metadata and a short "grounding" summary. Guardrails (prompt injection + tool misuse): Tool allow-list only includes retrieve + (optional) summarize; no arbitrary HTTP/file execution. Tool timeouts enforced (per-tool and overall request deadline). Strict JSON schema validation for tool inputs/outputs (fail closed with safe error messages). Prompt injection mitigations: retrieval results are treated as untrusted; we strip/normalize control sequences, remove markdown code-fences that attempt to introduce new system instructions, and wrap retrieved text in a clearly delimited "context" section. We also add an instruction layer that explicitly forbids following instructions inside retrieved documents. Sensitive-data handling: retrieved chunks are redacted in logs by default; template docs call out PII handling and recommended redaction/hashing patterns for production. Limits: max tool calls, max retrieved tokens budget, and max context window budget are configured to avoid runaway costs. Observability: All requests include request_id + tenant_id propagation and emit trace attributes for route/model, plus token usage breakdown (prompt_tokens/completion_tokens/total_tokens) when available from SDK response. Logs are structured JSON with correlation IDs. Errors are normalized into a small taxonomy (timeout, rate_limited, upstream, validation, tool_error). What’s included (high-level): New template directory: templates/combined-rag-agent/ (Python + TypeScript variants kept in parallel structure, matching our catalog naming). Python implementation: FastAPI service exposes POST /chat with streaming support, plus a small "ingest" CLI for loading docs and a vector adapter interface; retrieval tool is an adapter over the vector client. TypeScript implementation: Express-based API with streaming; retrieval tool shares the same contract and uses the shared SDK helper for retries/timeouts. Shared contracts: JSON schemas for tool input/output, shared prompt fragments, and a small "policy" module implementing allow-list + call budget + timeout wrapper. Docs: README with local run, environment variables, safe defaults checklist, and a section "How this maps to Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private" (networking, audit logs, and where to attach OTel exporters). Tests: basic unit tests for schema validation + injection sanitization; a small "golden path" smoke test that runs an agent query requiring retrieval and verifies tool-call path taken at least once. Configuration: ENV contract matches other templates (REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_BASE_URL, REDWOOD_MODEL, REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, LOG_LEVEL, TEMPLATE_TENANT_ID, TEMPLATE_ROUTE). Notable design choices / tradeoffs: We intentionally keep the agent orchestration minimal (no custom framework). The focus is showing safe patterns, not maximal autonomy. Retrieval is the only default tool in v1. Additional tools should be added behind explicit allow-lists and with schema + timeouts. Injection hardening is pragmatic: we sanitize and delimit retrieved text and add explicit instruction hierarchy; we do not attempt full content filtering. Follow-ups are tracked in ENG-2846 (dashboards pack) and ENG-2848 (CI smoke tests against staging). Files/areas changed (representative): templates/combined-rag-agent/python/app/main.py (FastAPI route, streaming, correlation IDs) templates/combined-rag-agent/python/app/agent/loop.py (planner/executor, tool budget) templates/combined-rag-agent/python/app/tools/retrieve.py (retrieval tool + adapter) templates/combined-rag-agent/python/app/security/injection.py (document sanitization, delimiting) templates/combined-rag-agent/python/schemas/*.json (tool I/O schemas) templates/combined-rag-agent/typescript/src/server.ts (Express route + streaming) templates/combined-rag-agent/typescript/src/agent/* (orchestration) templates/combined-rag-agent/README.md (setup + production notes) shared/telemetry/* (trace attributes + log field helpers reused by templates) Example snippet (Python tool wrapper): def call_tool(name, payload, *, timeout_ms): if name not in ALLOWED_TOOLS: raise ToolPolicyError(f"tool_not_allowed:{name}") validate_json_schema(payload, TOOL_INPUT_SCHEMAS[name]) with deadline(timeout_ms): result = TOOLS[name](payload) validate_json_schema(result, TOOL_OUTPUT_SCHEMAS[name]) return result Review notes / conversation highlights: Dana Lo: Requested aligning env var names with the TypeScript template contract (TEMPLATE_TENANT_ID vs TENANT_ID) and adding a hard cap on tool calls per request. Addressed in 8c2d1f1 (renamed env vars; added MAX_TOOL_CALLS default=3). Monica Patel: Asked to use the standardized SDK retry/timeout helper rather than ad-hoc retry loops; also requested we propagate traceparent if present. Addressed in 2a9f4b7 (switched to shared sdk_helpers; added header passthrough). Marcus Lin (Security): Requested clearer prompt instruction hierarchy (system/developer/user separation), plus logging guidance to avoid printing retrieved raw docs. Addressed in 61d1a20 (prompt fragments refactor; default log redaction; added README security section). Logan Wright: Requested adding required trace attributes per telemetry contract v1 and avoiding high-cardinality span attributes (no raw query string). Addressed in 34f0b99 (added route/model/tenant/request_id attrs; removed query from spans; added hash_query for debugging in debug logs only). Wei Chen: Requested README edits for clarity and a short "FAQ: Why retrieve is a tool" section. Addressed in a1f3d65. CI: Checks: lint (py/ts) ✅, unit tests ✅, typecheck ✅, template build ✅. One transient failure on windows-node due to line endings; rerun passed after .gitattributes tweak (commit f27c0aa). Merge: Squash merge into main after approvals from DX + Security + Observability. Linked work: ENG-2844 (combined template), ENG-2845 (telemetry contract compliance).
commits: Add combined-rag-agent template scaffold (python + ts) with shared folder layout
Implement planner/executor agent loop with tool-call budget + timeouts
Add retrieval tool + vector adapter interface and ingest CLI
Add prompt injection mitigations (sanitization + context delimiting) and safe prompt fragments
Wire OpenTelemetry traces + structured logs with request_id/tenant_id correlation
Docs: README for local run, env var contract, Hosted/Dedicated/Private notes
Tests: schema validation, injection sanitization, and golden-path agent+retrieve test
CI fixes: line endings + lint config alignment
